exposure: Opioid prescription filled from 7 days before delivery to 8 weeks after delivery (childbirth period)
Specific opioid medication exposure (e.g., tramadol, oxycodone)
outcome: Persistent postpartum opioid use (defined as opioid use disorder diagnosis or at least one filled opioid prescription in two or more calendar quarters from 8 weeks to 14 months postpartum)
cohort: The study included 172,839 births from 2015-2021 Pennsylvania Medicaid claims involving women aged 19-50 years with vaginal or cesarean delivery and Medicaid enrollment for at least 10 months during the postpartum year.
finding: Opioid use for childbirth pain management was significantly associated with an increased risk of persistent postpartum opioid use, particularly among opioid-naive patients and those exposed to tramadol.
